# Walter Blythe

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Walter is considered the handsomest of the Ingleside children, possessing straight black hair and finely modelled features. He features very wonderful, dark gray eyes that possess great depth, joy, and sorrow. He does not physically resemble any of his known relatives.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c4 P23](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0023)_

## Personality

Walter is an imaginative, daydreaming boy who inherits his mother's vivid imagination and passionate love of beauty. Possessing a strong dramatic instinct, he loves ghost stories, reading mythologies, and reciting poetry. He often takes blame upon himself and can exercise a quiet power over his friends when playing on their feelings with stories. Though quiet and prone to staying out of schoolboy sports and fights, he possesses an intense inner resolve when pushed to defend others.

_Sources: [v5 c3 P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c8 P12](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0012), [v5 c8 P27](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0027), [v5 c11 P1](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0001), [v5 c11 P45](../source/v05-c11.md#nw-v05-c11-p0045), [v5 c12 P26](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0026), [v5 c17 P16](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0016), [v5 c17 P56](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0056), [v5 c29 P8](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0008)_

## History

Walter grows up at Ingleside as one of the Blythe children, frequently spending his evenings playing with his siblings and companions in Rainbow Valley. Due to his quiet nature, preference for reading poetry, and avoidance of fisticuffs, he is considered 'girly' by the boys at Glen St. Mary school, though he earns a degree of respect for his eloquent way of speaking. He writes his own poetry in secret, sharing his writings only with his sister Di and looking up to 'Uncle' Paul Irving as a poetic model. After suffering from a severe toothache, he admits his deep hatred and fear of physical pain to Faith Meredith. Later, when Dan Reese insults Walter's mother, Walter overcomes his intense dread of being hurt and challenges Dan to a fight, successfully grappling with him after school while wearing Faith's blue ribbon. He also forms a close friendship with the minister, John Meredith, sharing deep talks with him in Rainbow Valley.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P1](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0001), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 c3 P17](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0017), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c16 P8](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0008), [v5 c16 P14](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0014), [v5 c17 P16](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0016), [v5 c17 P31](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0031), [v5 c17 P41](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0041), [v5 c17 P56](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0056)_
